episode_title: Build Smart, Grow Steady: The Realities of Scaling an Aesthetic Practice

real_qa.q: How did Dr. Judith Borger start Concierge Medical Arts while working full-time as an ER doctor?
real_qa.r: Dr. Borger started with a $40,000 budget as a side business while maintaining full-time ER work. She initially sublet a room from a salon and spa on her days off, then transitioned to a small medical office suite with two treatment rooms in a medical office complex. As the practice grew, she gradually reduced her ER shifts from full-time to 10 shifts per month, then worked part-time for a long time, eventually hiring another physician to fill those hours. She reinvested all initial earnings back into the business and built incrementally rather than attempting to acquire all equipment and services at once.
real_qa.requete: start aesthetics practice side business full-time job

real_qa.q: What was Dr. Judith Borger's initial capital investment to launch Concierge Medical Arts?
real_qa.r: Dr. Borger started Concierge Medical Arts with a $40,000 budget. She rejected the common industry advice that required a million dollars to start an aesthetic practice, choosing instead to build incrementally. She reinvested all money earned back into the business rather than taking immediate profits, allowing her to gradually acquire equipment and hire staff over time.
real_qa.requete: starting budget aesthetic practice Concierge Medical Arts

real_qa.q: How did Dr. Judith Borger's practice recover when COVID-19 shut down Concierge Medical Arts in North Carolina?
real_qa.r: During COVID-19 lockdown in North Carolina, Dr. Borger pivoted by conducting COVID vaccine and therapeutic research instead of aesthetic services. She served as Principal Investigator for Novavax, Moderna, Regeneron, and other COVID vaccine and therapeutic trials, using the research income to continue paying her three employees (a nurse, esthetician, and virtual assistant) despite the practice being closed. She maintained good cash reserves which enabled her to sustain payroll through the shutdown.
real_qa.requete: COVID-19 aesthetic practice closure pivot research

real_qa.q: What percentage of Dr. Judith Borger's patient schedule was canceled during the government shutdown at Fort Bragg?
real_qa.r: During the government shutdown last year, 40% of Dr. Borger's schedule was canceled the Monday after employees had not been paid. She attributed this to Fayetteville being located at Fort Bragg, the world's largest military installation, where the majority of residents are government employees.
real_qa.requete: government shutdown Fort Bragg patient cancellations 40%

real_qa.q: What was the cost of the most expensive medical device Dr. Judith Borger invested in for Concierge Medical Arts?
real_qa.r: Dr. Borger invested over $200,000 in her most expensive device at Concierge Medical Arts, purchasing it just a couple of months before COVID-19 shut down the practice. She had also recently moved into a new location with buildout costs and had to manage these significant capital investments through the pandemic closure.

guest.bio_context: Dr. Judith Borger is a board-certified physician and ER doctor by training who transitioned into medical aesthetics entrepreneurship. She founded Concierge Medical Arts, a cash-only medical aesthetics practice in Fayetteville, North Carolina offering full-spectrum non-surgical treatments. She hosts The Aesthetic Doctor podcast, ranked in the top 5% global podcasts in health, beauty, and wellness, and is certified in Martha Beck's Wayfinder coaching method. She has authored and co-authored close to 50 peer-reviewed articles and serves as a life and business coach, helping entrepreneurs align their businesses with their core missions.
